title: Uncomplicated Malaria
tocPath: APPROACH TO PATIENTS WITH EMERGENCY CONDITIONS

blocks.text: Uncomplicated malaria is defined as symptomatic malaria without signs of severity or evidence (clinical or laboratory) of vital organ dysfunction.
Fever, Headache, Joint pains, Malaise, Vomiting, Diarrhoea, Body ache, body weakness, Poor appetite, Pallor, enlarged spleen

blocks.text: The recommended investigations are: Quality malaria microscopy or quality malaria Rapid Diagnostic Tests (mRDT)
It is compulsory to test and confirm all suspected malaria patients. Give antimalarial only to those who test positive.

runs.text: It is compulsory to test and confirm all suspected malaria patients. Give antimalarial

blocks.text: In cases where non-response to malaria treatment (treatment failure) is suspected in patients who initially tested positive, microscopy is the recommended laboratory procedure as mRDTs are not recommended because parasite antigens persist up to 4 weeks after parasitaemia has cleared.

blocks.text: Continue with feeding and fluid intake
Followed up immediately if the condition worsens or on the fourth day if symptoms persist.
Drug of choice for treatment of uncomplicated malaria is:
Common fixed dose (FDC) formulations of Artemether +Lumefantrine (ALU):

Artesunate-Amodiaquine (ASAQ) is a another first-line medicine of choice for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria. Its therapeutic efficacy, remains above 90% (evaluated at Day 28, with PCR correction, following WHO standard protocol.

The alternative medicines for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria (where there is no response to ALU and ASAQ or whenever they are contraindicated) is a fixed dose formulation of Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine.

Treatment of Malaria using ACT plus Primaquine.
To reduce transmissibility of treated malaria infection in a very low transmission area. A single low dose of 0.25mg/kg primaquine with ACT is given to malaria patients.

runs.text: To reduce transmissibility of treated malaria infection in a very low transmission area. A single low dose of 0.25mg/kg primaquine with ACT is given to malaria patients.

blocks.text: The addition of a low single dose of Primaquine (0.25mg/kg maximum of 15mg in adults) to ACTs should be given to all eligible patients because it affects the transmissibility of mature gametocytes of P. falciparum by minimizing further transmission of the disease.

runs.text: eligible patients because it affects the transmissibility of mature gametocytes of P. falciparum by minimizing further transmission of the disease.

blocks.text: Formulation: Primaquine is available in the formulation of tablets 7.5 mg and 15 mg. Dosage:
A: primaquine single 0.25mg/kg/dose (Table 5.5) should be given to all qualified patients with parasitological confirmed malaria
Primaquine should be given on the first day of treatment in addition to an ACT, preferably under Directly Observed Therapy
Not recommended in pregnant women, women in the first 6 months of breastfeeding and children less than 6 months of age.
Haemolytic Anemia, especially in G6PD individuals, is the major adverse event reported. Although, single low dose of Primaquine is considered to be safe.
